legend: You are given an undirected tree with n%%ZSMJ0%% vertices, labeled from 0%%ZSMJ1%% to n−1%%ZSMJ2%%. The tree has n−1%%ZSMJ3%% edges and is connected and acyclic.
Your task is to select exactly k%%ZSMJ4%% vertices (2≤k≤n%%ZSMJ5%%) such that the minimum MEX%%ZSMJ6%% value over all paths between two chosen vertices is maximized.

For any two vertices u%%ZSMJ7%% and v%%ZSMJ8%%, define Puv%%ZSMJ9%% as the set of vertex labels that appear on the unique simple path between them. The function MEX(Puv)%%ZSMJ10%% is defined as the smallest non-negative integer that does not appear in Puv%%ZSMJ11%%.
Formally, for a chosen set of vertices S%%ZSMJ12%% with |S|=k%%ZSMJ13%%, we define: f(S)=minu,v∈S,u≠vMEX(Puv).%%ZSMJ14%%
Your goal is to maximize f(S)%%ZSMJ15%% over all valid choices of S%%ZSMJ16%%.
For each integer k%%ZSMJ17%% from 2%%ZSMJ18%% to n%%ZSMJ19%%, compute the maximum possible value of f(S)%%ZSMJ20%%.

The next n−1%%ZSMJ25%% lines each contain two integers u%%ZSMJ26%% and v%%ZSMJ27%% (0≤u,v<n)%%ZSMJ28%%, representing an undirected edge between nodes u%%ZSMJ29%% and v%%ZSMJ30%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all n%%ZSMJ31%% over all test cases does not exceed 106%%ZSMJ32%%.
output: For each test case, print n−1%%ZSMJ33%% integers. The i%%ZSMJ34%%-th integer should represent the maximum possible value of the minimum MEX%%ZSMJ35%% when choosing k=i+1%%ZSMJ36%% nodes.
